summary.title: Recovering at home after pneumonia
summary.what_happened: Maria was treated in the hospital for community-acquired pneumonia, a lung infection. Her oxygen levels improved after antibiotics and breathing treatments, and she is stable enough to continue recovery at home.
summary.recovery_goal: Finish the antibiotic course, use breathing medicine only as directed, monitor symptoms closely, and follow up with primary care in 3-5 days.

today.task: Start or continue amoxicillin/clavulanate exactly as prescribed.
today.why_it_matters: Finishing the antibiotic course helps treat the pneumonia and lowers the chance of symptoms returning.

today.task: Use the albuterol inhaler only if wheezing or shortness of breath occurs.
today.why_it_matters: The inhaler is for breathing symptoms and should be used according to the discharge instructions.

today.task: Rest, drink fluids, and avoid smoking or secondhand smoke.
today.why_it_matters: These steps support lung recovery after pneumonia.

medications.name: Amoxicillin/clavulanate
medications.timing: By mouth twice daily for 5 days
medications.instructions: Take exactly as prescribed and finish the full course even if feeling better.
medications.caution: Call the clinician for rash, severe diarrhea, or inability to keep fluids down.

medications.name: Albuterol inhaler
medications.purpose: Helps with wheezing or shortness of breath
medications.instructions: Use only as directed for breathing symptoms.
medications.caution: Seek urgent help for severe trouble breathing, blue lips, confusion, fainting, or oxygen below 90%.

medications.name: Acetaminophen
medications.timing: By mouth every 6 hours as needed
medications.instructions: Do not exceed 3,000 mg per day.
medications.caution: Ask a doctor or pharmacist before combining with other products that may contain acetaminophen.

red_flags.symptom: Severe trouble breathing, chest pain, blue lips, confusion, fainting, or oxygen below 90%
Fever above 101.5 F, worsening cough, inability to keep fluids down, rash, severe diarrhea, or symptoms not improving after 48-72 hours
Mild tiredness or cough that is gradually improving
red_flags.action: Monitor symptoms and mention them at follow-up if they persist.

follow_ups.task: Schedule or attend primary care follow-up.
follow_ups.reason: To confirm pneumonia symptoms are improving and review recovery.

follow_ups.task: Ask whether repeat chest imaging is needed.
follow_ups.timeframe: At follow-up or sooner if symptoms worsen
follow_ups.reason: The discharge note says repeat imaging may be considered if symptoms do not improve.

questions_for_clinician: Should Maria avoid any over-the-counter medicines while taking these prescriptions?
What should she do if fever returns after starting antibiotics?
Does she need repeat chest imaging after recovery?
When can she return to normal activity?
